info.title: NaN API
info.description:
Open models on a shared EU inference cluster. Zero logs.

The NaN API is OpenAI-compatible: predictable, resource-oriented URLs, JSON request and response bodies, and standard HTTP verbs and status codes. Point any OpenAI SDK at our base URL and your existing code keeps working. Change the base URL and the API key, and that's it.

One schema across every model, so you only learn the API once. Change the `model` field to switch models; everything else stays the same.

- Base URL: `https://api.nan.builders/v1`
- OpenAPI spec: this document. Import it into Postman, Insomnia, or your own tooling.

If you use the [Helmcode](https://helmcode.com) enterprise service, the base URL is `https://api.helmcode.com/v1` instead. Every other endpoint is identical.

## Authentication

Every inference request authenticates with an API key, sent as a Bearer token:

```
Authorization: Bearer $NAN_API_KEY
```

You must be a NaN community member. Generate your key from user settings, under "API Keys", on the [platform](https://cloud.nan.builders/). The key is personal and non-transferable. Keep it secret: never embed one in client-side code or commit it to source control. Requests must go over HTTPS; calls over plain HTTP fail.

### Platform tokens

For scripts that only manage [Runs](#tag/runs), [Automations](#tag/automations) and [Approvals](#tag/approvals), and list your [Workspaces](#tag/workspaces), create a **platform token** (`nan_pat_...`) under "Tokens" in your settings, and send it the same way: `Authorization: Bearer $NAN_TOKEN`. An API key works on both inference and these endpoints. Each endpoint lists the credentials it accepts.

A platform token carries **scopes**, and each endpoint names the one it needs: `runs` (runs and approvals), `workspaces:read`, `automations:read` (read automations, templates, triggers and deliveries) and `automations:run` (run an existing automation). New tokens get `runs` and `workspaces:read`. A token without the scope gets `403`:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "This platform token does not have the \"automations:run\" scope this endpoint requires. Create a token with that scope in the Tokens section of Settings at cloud.nan.builders.",
    "type": "permission_error",
    "param": null,
    "code": "token_scope_denied"
  }
}
```

A platform token never works for inference: the model endpoints answer `401`:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "Platform tokens (nan_pat_) cannot be used for inference. Use an inference API key (sk-) instead. Platform tokens only work on the platform API (/v1/runs and GET /api/workspaces).",
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "param": null,
    "code": "token_not_valid_for_inference"
  }
}
```

### Browser sign-in

Some actions need you signed in through your browser at [cloud.nan.builders](https://cloud.nan.builders/), and no API key, platform token or CLI session can do them: approving a run, creating, editing or deleting automations and their triggers, writing secrets, and creating a token with an `automations:` scope. Through the API they answer `403`:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "This action needs a browser session: sign in at cloud.nan.builders in your browser and try again from there. CLI sessions, API keys and platform tokens cannot approve runs, change automations or secrets, or create tokens with automations scopes.",
    "type": "permission_error",
    "param": null,
    "code": "browser_session_required"
  }
}
```

## Making requests

The API is OpenAI-compatible, so point an official OpenAI SDK at our base URL and change nothing else:

```python
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key="$NAN_API_KEY",
    base_url="https://api.nan.builders/v1",
)

resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="deepseek-v4-flash",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
)
print(resp.choices[0].message.content)
```

## Streaming

Chat responses can stream token-by-token. Set `"stream": true` on `/chat/completions` and the response arrives as Server-Sent Events: each event is a `data:` line carrying a `chat.completion.chunk`, with the new text in `choices[0].delta.content`. A final `data: [DONE]` line ends the stream. `/chat/completions` streams incrementally on every chat model. `/responses` streams incrementally on `deepseek-v4-flash`, `glm5.3-flash`, `qwen3.8-flash`, `mimo-v2.6-flash` and `glm5.3`; on `qwen3.6` and `gemma4` it holds the whole answer and sends it in one burst at the end.

## Rate limits

{{RATE_LIMITS}}

Image endpoints run on their own budget, separate from the model endpoints: 20 requests per minute and 100 requests per month. The usage endpoint is metered separately too: {{USAGE_RATE_LIMIT}} requests per minute per member. Exceed any limit and you get a `429`.

## Errors

NaN uses conventional HTTP status codes: `2xx` on success, `4xx` for a problem with the request (a missing parameter, an invalid key, an unavailable model) and `5xx` for a server-side error. Every error returns a JSON body in the OpenAI shape:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "The model 'foo' does not exist.",
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "param": "model",
    "code": "model_not_found"
  }
}
```

`message` is human-readable, `param` names the offending field when applicable, and `code` is a short machine-readable string you can branch on.

| Status | Meaning | `code` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `400` | Invalid or malformed parameter (`param` says which); content blocked by the safety filter; a `max_tokens` above what the model can generate (a generic "Invalid request" message today); or a request that does not fit the model's context window. On the models hosted on the cluster (`qwen3.6`, `gemma4`) the overflow message is "Context length exceeded for model '...'" with the model's limit; on the other models it is usually that text, but it can arrive as the generic "Invalid request. Check your request parameters." | `"400"` (with `type: invalid_request_error`) · `content_policy_violation` |
| `401` | Missing or invalid API key, or a key whose tier does not reach the requested model (`glm5.3`): "This API key does not have access to the requested model", `type: auth_error`. Measured 2026-09-12. A platform token (`nan_pat_...`) sent to an inference endpoint answers `token_not_valid_for_inference`. | `invalid_api_key` · `token_not_valid_for_inference` |
| `402` | The token allowance is spent on a model that carries one. Not retryable: the counter returns to zero when that model's quota period does, the calendar month for the models counted per month and your billing period for `glm5.3`. | `monthly_cap_reached` |
| `403` | Your tier can't access this endpoint. Image generation requires inference membership. A model your tier cannot reach answers `401`, not this. On the platform endpoints: a platform token without the scope the endpoint needs, or an action that needs a [browser sign-in](#description/browser-sign-in). | `tier_restricted` · `token_scope_denied` · `browser_session_required` |
| `404` | The requested model doesn't exist. | `model_not_found` |
| `429` | Rate limit hit (`rpm_limit`, `max_parallel_requests`), the rolling 4h token budget of `glm5.3`, or a quota exhausted. | `rate_limit_exceeded` · `insufficient_quota` · `quota_exceeded` |
| `500` | Something went wrong on our side (includes upstream model errors). | (none) |
| `524` | Timeout, typical with large audio files on `/audio/transcriptions`. | (none) |

Retry `429` and `5xx` responses with exponential backoff. Don't retry `400`, `401`, `403`, or `404` blindly (a context overflow is not retried automatically either: shorten the input or pick a model with a larger window): they'll fail the same way every time until you change the request. `402` cannot be fixed by repetition either: it clears when that model's quota period resets.

## Model catalog

Every endpoint takes a `model` id. Capabilities vary by model:

| Model | Use for | Capabilities |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `deepseek-v4-flash` | Chat, vision, reasoning | Streaming, tool calling, reasoning, image input, 1M-token context. 3B tokens/month per member |
| `mimo-v2.6-flash` | Chat, vision, audio | Streaming, tool calling, reasoning, image input, audio input, 1M-token context. 1.0B tokens/month per member |
| `qwen3.8-flash` | Chat, vision, agents | Streaming, tool calling, reasoning (on by default), vision, 1M-token context. 500M tokens/month per member |
| `glm5.3-flash` | Chat, vision, agents | Streaming, tool calling, reasoning, vision, 1M-token context. 2B tokens/month per member |
| `qwen3.6` | Chat, agents | Streaming, tool calling, vision, reasoning (opt-out, returns `reasoning_content`) |
| `gemma4` | Chat, vision, agents | Streaming, tool calling, vision, reasoning (opt-in) |
| `glm5.3` | Coding, long-horizon agents | Streaming, tool calling, reasoning trace, image, audio and video input, 1M-token context. Premium tier only |
| `qwen3-embedding` | Embeddings | 4096-dimension vectors |
| `rerank` | RAG reranking | Qwen3-Reranker-8B, 100+ languages |
| `kokoro` | Text-to-speech | Multiple voices and audio formats |
| `whisper` | Speech-to-text | Transcription with word/segment timestamps |
| `flux-2-klein` | Image generation | Text-to-image and image-to-image |
| `qwen-image-2.1` | Image generation (text→image) | 512-1280 px, 1-4 per request, seed 0-2147483647. 100 images/month per member (shared pool with flux-2-klein) |

`glm5.3` is served only to keys on the GLM 5.3 premium tier; every other model is available to any inference member. Call [List models](#tag/Models) for the exact set available to your key.

## Versioning & compatibility

The API tracks the OpenAI API surface, so OpenAI SDKs and tools work against `https://api.nan.builders/v1` unchanged. This reference documents the stable public `/v1` endpoints, plus the two read-only [Workspaces](#tag/workspaces) endpoints under `/api/workspaces`, and we add capabilities without breaking existing fields.

tags.name: Chat
tags.description: Chat completions, the main conversational endpoint.

tags.name: Runs
tags.description: Give an agent (Pi, Pi + Gentle Shell or Hermes) a task inside one of your workspaces and follow it. A run keeps going if the client disconnects. Accepts a member API key or a platform token with the `runs` scope. Guide: [Agent runs](https://nan.builders/docs/runs).

tags.name: Automations
tags.description: Read and run the automations you set up in the portal: saved agent tasks that webhooks, schedules or your own calls start. Reading needs a platform token with `automations:read`, running one `automations:run` (or your API key). Creating, editing and deleting automations and their triggers is done in the portal, signed in through your browser: those routes answer `403 browser_session_required` to API keys and platform tokens. Webhooks themselves arrive at `https://api.nan.builders/hooks/<token>`, signed by the sender. Guides: [Automations](https://nan.builders/docs/automations), [Webhooks and schedules](https://nan.builders/docs/webhooks).

tags.name: Approvals
tags.description: The actions your automation runs propose, and the ones waiting for your approval. List them, read a proposal and its diff, and reject. Approving is done only in the portal, signed in through your browser (`POST /v1/runs/{id}/approve` answers `403 browser_session_required` to API keys and platform tokens), so nothing a script or an agent holds can approve. Guide: [Automations](https://nan.builders/docs/automations#approve-or-reject-a-proposal).

tags.name: Workspaces
tags.description: Read-only access to your own workspaces, for scripts that need a workspace's name, id or status. Served at `https://api.nan.builders/api/workspaces`, outside `/v1`, to bearer credentials only (no cookies, no browser CORS). Creating, starting, stopping and deleting workspaces is done from the platform, not from this API. Guide: [Workspaces](https://nan.builders/docs/workspaces).

post.description: Creates a model response for the given chat conversation. Compatible with OpenAI's Chat Completions API.

model.description:
Model id. See [List models](#tag/Models) for what your key can use. Chat models are `deepseek-v4-flash`, `mimo-v2.6-flash`, `qwen3.8-flash`, `glm5.3-flash`, `qwen3.6`, `gemma4` and `glm5.3`.

`glm5.3` requires a key on the GLM 5.3 premium tier; other keys get `401` `auth_error` ("This API key does not have access to the requested model"), and do not see it in [List models](#tag/Models) either. The rest are available to every inference member.

messages.description: The conversation so far, oldest first. `content` is a string, or an array of parts (`text` + `image_url`) for vision input on every chat model: `deepseek-v4-flash`, `mimo-v2.6-flash`, `qwen3.8-flash`, `glm5.3-flash`, `qwen3.6`, `gemma4` and `glm5.3`.

max_tokens.description: Maximum number of tokens to generate. A value above what the model can generate is rejected with a generic `400`. A request that does not fit the model's context window is rejected with a `400`: "Context length exceeded for model '...'" on `qwen3.6` and `gemma4`, usually the same text (sometimes the generic "Invalid request") on the other models. On `deepseek-v4-flash` a smaller value is raised to 16384 so the reasoning fits, so a prompt within 16384 tokens of its 1,048,576-token window is rejected with a `400` even with a small `max_tokens`.

temperature.description: Sampling temperature. Higher is more random, lower more deterministic.

top_p.description: Nucleus sampling: only consider the top `top_p` probability mass.

stream.description: When `true`, the reply arrives as Server-Sent Events: each `data:` line is a `chat.completion.chunk` with new text in `choices[0].delta.content`, ending with `data: [DONE]`.

tools.description: Functions the model may call (OpenAI function schema). When it calls one, the reply carries `choices[0].message.tool_calls` and `finish_reason: "tool_calls"`. Validated on `qwen3.6`.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning depth. Per model: `glm5.3` and `glm5.3-flash` accept `low`, `medium`, `high` and `max` — deeper means the model reasons longer before answering. `qwen3.6` and `gemma4` accept `none` or `minimal` (no reasoning phase at all) and `low`, `medium`, `high`, `max`, which cap the reasoning phase at 2,048 / 8,192 / 16,384 / 32,768 tokens. `deepseek-v4-flash` reasons adaptively per request: the parameter is accepted and has no effect. The remaining chat models accept the parameter and manage their own depth. The reasoning trace arrives in `message.reasoning_content`. A value a model cannot apply is never rejected. Details: [Models](https://nan.builders/docs/models).

chat_template_kwargs.description: Reasoning toggle for `qwen3.6`/`gemma4`: `{ "enable_thinking": boolean }`. In OpenAI SDKs, pass it inside `extra_body`.

premium_tier.description: `glm5.3` is served only to keys on the GLM 5.3 premium tier. Same request shape as any other model, only `model` changes. A key without the tier gets `401` `auth_error`: "This API key does not have access to the requested model". It reads like a broken key and is not.

messages.content: Refactor this function and explain the trade-offs.

200.description: The chat completion. When `stream: false` the body is a single `chat.completion` (`application/json`). When `stream: true` the body is a `text/event-stream` of `chat.completion.chunk` events ending with `data: [DONE]`.

message.content: Hello! How can I help you?

    api_key="$NAN_API_KEY",
    base_url="https://api.nan.builders/v1",

    cast_to=object,

post.description:
Creates a model response using the OpenAI-style Responses API. Models: `deepseek-v4-flash`, `glm5.3-flash`, `qwen3.8-flash`, `mimo-v2.6-flash`, `qwen3.6`, `gemma4`, `glm5.3`. On `deepseek-v4-flash` the `output` array carries a `reasoning` item before the `message`.

Streaming (`stream: true`) depends on the model. `deepseek-v4-flash`, `glm5.3-flash`, `qwen3.8-flash`, `mimo-v2.6-flash` and `glm5.3` stream incrementally, with the full event sequence: `response.created`, the reasoning summary deltas, `response.output_text.delta` as the answer is generated, and `response.completed`. On `qwen3.6` and `gemma4` the answer is held until it is complete and then arrives in one burst (`response.output_text.delta` events followed by `response.completed`); for token-by-token streaming on those two, use [Create chat completion](#tag/Chat) with `stream: true`.

input.description: The input: a single string, or an array of messages in the Responses format.

stream.description: Stream the response as Server-Sent Events. Incremental only on `deepseek-v4-flash`; see the description above.

max_output_tokens.description: The maximum number of output tokens. Default 65536 on `qwen3.6`.

instructions.description: System-level instructions that steer the model.

post.description:
Creates one or more images from a text prompt (text-to-image). Model: `flux-2-klein`.

Requires `inference`-tier membership (`403` otherwise). Image endpoints are rate-limited separately from chat: 20 requests per minute and 100 requests per month per user. These don't consume your chat token budget. `stream: true` is not supported. For OpenAI SDK compatibility, `quality`, `style`, `background`, `moderation`, `output_format`, `output_compression`, and `user` are accepted but ignored.

prompt.description: A text description of the image to generate.
prompt.example: A lighthouse at sunset over cliffs, cinematic style

model.description: The image model: `flux-2-klein` (default) or `qwen-image-2.1`. An unknown model returns `404`.

n.description: The number of images to generate (1–4). Values above 4 return `400`.

size.description: "WIDTHxHEIGHT". Each side divisible by 16 and between 256 and 1536, aspect ratio 1:3–3:1. `auto` or omitted → `1024x1024`.

response_format.description: `url` returns a temporary link (~60 min); `b64_json` returns inline base64 bytes.

seed.description: NaN extension: base seed for reproducibility (in OpenAI SDKs, pass via `extra_body`).

guidance.description: NaN extension: FLUX guidance scale (in OpenAI SDKs, pass via `extra_body`).

get.description:
The run's log, as a live stream or as JSON pages.

**Stream.** Send `Accept: text/event-stream` (with `curl`, add `-N`). The server first replays every stored event after your resume point, then sends new ones as they happen. Frames:

- `id: <seq>` + `event: run_event` + `data: <RunEvent>`: one event of the log.
- `event: state` + `data: {"state", "error_code"}`: the run changed state.
- `event: end` + `data: <Run>`: the run is over, or waiting for your approval (`awaiting_approval`), and every event has been sent. The server closes the stream after it.
- `: hb`: a comment line every 15 seconds that keeps the connection open. Ignore it.

To resume after a dropped connection, send the last `id` you received as the `Last-Event-ID` header (it wins over `after`): you get the rest without gaps or repeats. A stream lasts at most 30 minutes; if it closes before `end`, reconnect with `Last-Event-ID`. Up to 10 open streams per member (`429 too_many_streams`).

**JSON pages.** Without that `Accept` header the same endpoint answers one page of events after `after`. Pass the page's `next_after` as `after` until `done` is `true`.

get.description:
One of your own workspaces, plus `env_var_keys`: the names (never the values) of the variables in its environment file. Only your own workspaces are returned: another member's workspace answers `404`, exactly like an id that does not exist.

Authentication: a member API key (`sk-...`) or a platform token (`nan_pat_...`). The key that lives inside a workspace is not accepted.

On `api.nan.builders` this route takes a bearer credential only: cookies are ignored, and there is no browser CORS support (`OPTIONS` answers `404`), so call it from a server or a script, not from a web page.

apiKey.description: Member API key (`sk-...`), from "API Keys" in your settings on the platform. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <api-key>`. It works on every inference endpoint, on the Runs, Automations and Approvals endpoints and on the two Workspaces endpoints (it cannot approve runs or change automations). Personal and non-transferable. The key that lives inside a workspace (the one its agents use) is refused by the Runs endpoints with `403 workspace_key_not_allowed`.

platformToken.description: Platform token (`nan_pat_...`), from "Tokens" in your settings on the platform. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It works only on the platform API: Runs (`/v1/runs...`), Automations (`/v1/automations...`), Approvals and the two Workspaces endpoints, and only where it carries the scope the endpoint names: `runs`, `workspaces:read`, `automations:read` or `automations:run`. A missing scope answers `403 token_scope_denied`. New tokens get `runs` and `workspaces:read` by default; a token with an `automations:` scope can only be created from a browser sign-in. It never works for inference: inference endpoints refuse it with `401 token_not_valid_for_inference`. It can never approve a run or change automations or secrets. Shown once when you create it; up to 10 active; expires after 30, 90 or 365 days, or never; revocable at any time. Any member with an active subscription can create one; creating runs still needs a plan with inference.

Model.description: An available model, in the OpenAI-compatible model shape.

id.description: The model's unique slug. Pass this value as the `model` field in your requests.

object.description: The object type, which is always `model`.

created.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) when the model became available.

owned_by.description: The organization that owns the model.

ContentPart.description: One part of a multimodal message. Use an array of these as `content` for vision input.

url.description: Public URL or `data:` URI of the image.

Message.description: A single message in a conversation. The `role` determines which other fields apply.

role.description: The role of the message author: `system`, `user`, `assistant`, or `tool`.

content.description: The contents of the message. A plain string, or an array of content parts for multimodal input. Can be `null` on an `assistant` message that only returns tool calls.

name.description: An optional name for the author of this message.

tool_calls.description: The tool calls generated by the model. Present on `assistant` messages when the model decides to invoke one or more tools.

tool_call_id.description: The id of the tool call this message answers. Required when `role` is `tool`.

reasoning_content.description: The model's reasoning trace. Present only for reasoning models; safe to display or ignore.

Tool.description: A function the model may call. Provide these in the request's `tools` array.

type.description: The type of the tool. Currently only `function` is supported.

name.description: The name of the function to call. Up to 64 characters; letters, digits, underscores and dashes. A name outside that pattern is rejected with a `400` before the request reaches the model, on every model.

description.description: What the function does, used by the model to decide when and how to call it. Be descriptive.

strict.description: Request that the generated arguments follow `parameters` exactly (fields, types and required keys); enforced where the model supports strict decoding. Combined with a forced `tool_choice`, it is the way to get schema-shaped output on `deepseek-v4-flash`, which returns arguments that follow the schema.

type.description: The root type of the schema. Must be `object`.

parameters.description: The parameters the function accepts, described as a JSON Schema object. When present, its root must be `"type": "object"`: a root of any other type, or with no `type`, is rejected with a `400` before the request reaches the model, on every model. A function that takes no arguments can omit `parameters` or send `{"type": "object", "properties": {}}`.

ToolChoice.description: Controls tool use: `"auto"` (default), `"none"`, `"required"`, or force one with `{ "type": "function", "function": { "name": "..." } }`.

ToolCall.description: A tool the model chose to call. Execute it, then send the result back in a `tool` message referencing `id`.

id.description: A unique id for this tool call. Pass it as `tool_call_id` in your follow-up `tool` message.

type.description: The type of the tool call. Always `function`.

name.description: The name of the function to call.

arguments.description: The function arguments as a JSON-encoded string. Parse and validate it before use; models can occasionally emit malformed JSON.

ResponseFormat.description:
Force structured output. What each mode guarantees:

- `json_object`: syntactically valid JSON only, NOT its shape. Describe the schema you want in the prompt. On `deepseek-v4-flash` the prompt must also contain the word JSON, otherwise `400`.
- `json_schema` with `strict: true`: the output is constrained to the schema (fields, types and required keys).

`json_schema` works on `qwen3.6` and `gemma4`. On `deepseek-v4-flash` it is rejected with a `400` before the request reaches the model; `json_object` still works there. For output that follows a schema on `deepseek-v4-flash`, define one function tool whose `parameters` is your JSON Schema (root `type: object`, `strict: true`), force it with `tool_choice: {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "..."}}` and read `choices[0].message.tool_calls[0].function.arguments`.

prompt_tokens.description: The number of tokens in the prompt (input).

completion_tokens.description: The number of tokens in the generated completion (output).

total_tokens.description: The total tokens used: `prompt_tokens` plus `completion_tokens`. This is what counts against your quota.

ChatCompletion.description: The model's response to a chat request. Represents a single, non-streamed completion.

id.description: A unique identifier for the completion.

created.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) when the completion was created.

model.description: The model that produced the completion.

index.description: The index of this choice in the `choices` array.

finish_reason.description: Why the model stopped: `stop` (natural end or a stop sequence), `length` (hit `max_tokens`), or `tool_calls` (the model called a tool).

choices.description: The list of completion choices. Contains a single choice unless you request more.

ChatCompletionChunk.description: One Server-Sent Event chunk when `stream: true`. New text arrives in `choices[0].delta.content`; the stream ends with `data: [DONE]`.

created.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) when the chunk was created. Identical across all chunks of one response.

delta.description: The incremental update for this chunk. `role` is set on the first chunk; `content` carries the new text to append.

finish_reason.description: `null` on intermediate chunks; set to the stop reason on the final content chunk.

Error.description: OpenAI-standard error envelope: a non-2xx HTTP status with a JSON body describing the problem.

Embedding.description: A single embedding vector for one input.

index.description: The position of this embedding in the request `input` array.

embedding.description: The embedding vector: a list of 4096 floats. Cosine similarity between vectors measures semantic closeness.

EmbeddingList.description: A list of embeddings, one per input.

model.description: The model used to create the embeddings.

data.description: The embeddings, in the same order as the request `input`.

index.description: The position of this document in the request `documents` array.

relevance_score.description: Relevance to the query, in the range [0, 1]. Higher is more relevant. Results are returned sorted by this, descending.

id.description: A unique identifier for the rerank request.

results.description: The documents, sorted by descending `relevance_score`. Each carries its original `index`.

Transcription.description: A transcription of the supplied audio.

language.description: The detected (or supplied) language, as an ISO-639-1 code.

duration.description: The audio duration in seconds. Present with `verbose_json`.

words.description: Per-word timestamps `[{ word, start, end, probability }]`. Populated only when `timestamp_granularities[]=word`.

ResponseObject.description: A response produced by the Responses API.

id.description: A unique identifier for the response.

created_at.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) when the response was created.

model.description: The model that produced the response.

output.description: The output items. May contain `reasoning` blocks (reasoning models) followed by a `message` block with the reply text in `content[].text`.

created.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) when the images were created.

data.description: The generated images. Each item has a `url` (default) or a `b64_json` payload, depending on `response_format`.

url.description: A temporary URL to the image, valid ~60 minutes. Returned when `response_format` is `url`.

b64_json.description: The base64-encoded image bytes. Returned when `response_format` is `b64_json`.

Completion.description: A completion for the provided prompt (legacy).

created.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) when the completion was created.

UsageReport.description: Your token usage for the requested window.

end_date.description: Last day of the effective window actually served, `YYYY-MM-DD`, after any clamping: the window your totals cover.

model.description: The model id, as in the Model catalog.

completion_tokens.description: Output tokens generated that day on that model.

completion_tokens.description: Total output tokens in the window.

prompt_tokens.description: Input tokens used on this model in the window.

completion_tokens.description: Output tokens generated on this model in the window.

api_requests.description: Requests made on this model in the window. Request counts are only available from 2026-09-02 onward; older days report `0`.

UsageAllTime.description: Your lifetime usage across all models.

api_requests.description: Total requests recorded for this member. Request counts are only available from 2026-09-02 onward; older days report `0`.

cached_at.description: When the all-time summary was last computed, as an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp.

error.description: Short error: `unauthorized`, `invalid session`, `session_required` or `workspace not found`.

CreateRunRequest.description: Body of `POST /v1/runs`. Unknown fields are refused with `400`.

workspace.description: Name or id of one of your workspaces.

agent.description: The agent: `pi` (Pi), `pi_gentle` (Pi + Gentle Shell: Pi started through gentle-shell) or `hermes` (Hermes). It must be installed in the workspace (see `run_agents` on the workspace), otherwise `409 agent_not_installed` with `param: "agent"`.

prompt.description: The task. 1 to 32768 bytes of UTF-8 (32 KiB), no NUL bytes. Called Task in the portal.
prompt.example: add tests for the date parser and make them pass

cwd.description: Working directory: an absolute path inside `/home/nan`, without `.` or `..` segments. Called Folder in the portal.

git_isolation.description: `null` (auto): when `cwd` is inside a git repository, the agent works on its own branch `nan-run/<first 8 characters of the run id>` in a separate worktree, commits its changes there and never pushes; outside a repository it works in the folder. `true`: always a separate branch (fails with `config_error` outside a repository). `false`: always in the folder. Called Separate branch in the portal.

timeout_seconds.description: Time limit. The run is stopped (`timed_out`) when it reaches it. Called Time limit in the portal.

model.description: Model for the agent. `null` uses the agent's own default.

trigger.description: Who started the run. Informational only.

RunArtifact.description: A file the agent left in its run's `artifacts/` folder.

path.description: Path relative to the run folder, under `artifacts/`.

RunResult.description: How the run ended, written once it is over. Text from the agent is data: render it as plain text.

summary.description: The agent's final answer, up to 4 KiB.

branch.description: The `nan-run/...` branch with the agent's commit, when it worked on a separate branch and changed something. `null` otherwise (with no changes the branch is deleted).

actions_applied.description: On an `apply` run: each action applied, in order. Empty otherwise.

ref.description: What the action produced: a commit, or the link of the pull request, comment or review.

Run.description: A run. Every response returns this object; `prompt` (the full task), `instructions` and `input` are only in `GET /v1/runs/{id}`.

agent.description: The agent: `pi` (Pi), `pi_gentle` (Pi + Gentle Shell: Pi started through gentle-shell) or `hermes` (Hermes).

trigger.description: What created the run: `api`, `cli` or `ui` (you, from the API, the CLI or the portal; a manual run of an automation is `api` or `ui`), `webhook` or `schedule` (an automation trigger), `approval` (the step that applies the actions you approved) or `automation` (the step that applies actions that need no approval).

state.description: `queued` waits for a free place (per-workspace and per-member limits), then `starting`, `running`, and one of the four final states. An automation run whose proposal needs your approval stops in `awaiting_approval` until you approve it (`succeeded`), reject it or it expires (`cancelled`).

prompt_preview.description: The first 200 characters of the task.

error_code.description: Why the run did not succeed, when there is a reason. For automation runs: `secrets_unavailable` or `secret_missing` (its secrets could not be delivered, so it did not start), `proposal_invalid` (the proposed actions were refused), `approval_rejected`, `approval_expired`, `action_failed` (an action could not be applied) and `automation_deleted` (deleted while the run was queued).

usage.description: Tokens the run used. Each field is `null` until it is known.

source.description: Where the counts come from: `litellm` (measured by the NaN gateway) or `agent` (reported by the agent).

phase.description: `run`: a run you start with `POST /v1/runs`. `propose`: an automation run, whose agent proposes actions instead of acting. `apply`: the step that applies a proposal's actions, with no agent.

inference.description: Where the run's inference comes from. Always NaN.

automation_id.description: The automation that created the run. `null` for runs you start with `POST /v1/runs`, and once the automation is deleted.

parent_run_id.description: On an `apply` run: the automation run whose proposal it applies.

apply_run_ids.description: On an automation run: the `apply` runs that applied its actions, in order.

approval.description: On an automation run that proposed actions: the proposal and where its approval stands. `null` otherwise.

instructions.description: The automation's instructions the run used. Only in `GET /v1/runs/{id}` of an automation run.

input.description: The event or input that started an automation run. Only in `GET /v1/runs/{id}`.

approval_kinds.description: On an automation run: the action kinds that needed approval when it started. `null` otherwise.

github_repo.description: On an automation run: the repository its actions act on.

trigger_depth.description: 0 for a run you start. 1 for a webhook or schedule run, one more for each run caused by another run (loop protection).

secrets.description: The secrets the run receives: variable names and who gets them, never values.

agent_finished_at.description: When the agent of an automation run finished, before any approval.

checkout.description: On an automation run (`phase: "propose"`) whose automation uses `checkout: "fresh"`: the commit it works on. `null` for every other run, apply runs included.

superseded_by.description: When a newer run for the same subject cancelled this one (`concurrency_policy: "supersede"`): that run's id. The run ends `cancelled` with `error_code: "cancelled"`.

sticky_pr_comment.description: On an automation run (`phase: "propose"`): whether its pull request comments edit the automation's one comment per pull request (`sticky_pr_comment` of the automation when the run started). `false` on other runs.

data.description: Newest first. `prompt` is not included: use `prompt_preview`.

next_cursor.description: Pass it as `cursor` for the next page. `null` on the last page.

RunEventDataStarted.description: `data` of a `started` event. The run started.

cwd.description: Where the agent works (inside the worktree when there is one).

worktree.description: The separate worktree, or `null` when the agent works in the folder.

branch.description: `nan-run/...` when there is a worktree, otherwise `null`.

checkout.description: Only on runs with a fresh checkout: the commit checked out.

RunEventDataLog.description: `data` of a `log` event. A line of output that is not a message.

RunEventDataMessage.description: `data` of a `message` event. Assistant text, sent incrementally: each event carries only its own chunk, and the last chunk of a message has `final: true` (its text may be empty). Concatenate the chunks to rebuild the message.

text.description: This chunk only, up to 16 KiB.

RunEventDataToolCall.description: `data` of a `tool_call` event. The agent called a tool.

RunEventDataToolResult.description: `data` of a `tool_result` event. What a tool answered. `id` matches its `tool_call`.

RunEventDataUsage.description: `data` of a `usage` event. Tokens used so far, as the agent reports them (cumulative).

RunEventDataError.description: `data` of an `error` event. Something went wrong.

RunEventDataTruncated.description: `data` of a `truncated` event. The run hit its event limit (20000 events) or size limit (16 MiB): later events are dropped, except `artifact`, `error` and `finished`.

RunEventDataFinished.description: `data` of a `finished` event. The run ended. Always the last event.

RunEvent.description: One event of a run's log. `type` says what `data` holds. Everything in `data` comes from the agent inside your workspace: treat it as untrusted text, never as markup. Secrets from the workspace's environment file are masked as `***`.

seq.description: 1, 2, 3... in order, per run. Use it to resume (`after`, `Last-Event-ID`).

type.description:
- `started`: The run started.
- `log`: A line of output that is not a message.
- `message`: Assistant text, sent incrementally: each event carries only its own chunk, and the last chunk of a message has `final: true` (its text may be empty). Concatenate the chunks to rebuild the message.
- `tool_call`: The agent called a tool.
- `tool_result`: What a tool answered. `id` matches its `tool_call`.
- `usage`: Tokens used so far, as the agent reports them (cumulative).
- `artifact`: A file the agent left in `artifacts/`.
- `error`: Something went wrong.
- `truncated`: The run hit its event limit (20000 events) or size limit (16 MiB): later events are dropped, except `artifact`, `error` and `finished`.
- `finished`: The run ended. Always the last event.
- `approval_required`: An automation run proposed actions that wait for your approval.
- `action`: One step of an `apply` run.

next_after.description: The last `seq` returned (or your `after` when the page is empty). Pass it as `after` for the next page.

done.description: `true` when the run is over and every event has been returned.

WorkspaceSlot.description: The purchased slot paying for the workspace.

Workspace.description: One of your workspaces. Never carries keys, environment values or agent configuration.

workspace_uuid.description: The workspace id. Accepted by `workspace` in `POST /v1/runs`.

name.description: Unique among your workspaces. Accepted by `workspace` in `POST /v1/runs`.

agent_selection.description: Agents and tools chosen for the workspace.

run_agents.description: The agents a run or an automation can use in this workspace, in display order (`pi`, `pi_gentle`, `hermes`). `pi` needs Pi installed, `pi_gentle` needs Pi and gentle-shell, `hermes` needs Hermes chosen for the workspace or installed. A run (from `POST /v1/runs` or from an automation) with an agent that is not listed here is refused with `409 agent_not_installed`. Empty when no agent is installed.

status.description: Runs can only be created while it is `running`.

ssh_command.description: The command to connect over SSH.

tier.description: Size. `free` is the Micro-sized workspace included with Premium.

state_reason.description: Why the workspace is not running normally, or `null`.

grace_until.description: When an open grace period ends (the data is deleted then), or `null`.

inference_attached.description: Whether the workspace has an inference key (never the key itself). Runs need it.

rescue.description: Rescue sessions during a grace period.

stale.description: `true` when the last snapshot is older than expected.

env_var_keys.description: Names of the variables in the workspace's environment file. Never the values.

RunInput.description: The untrusted input of an automation run. The agent receives it as data next to the automation's instructions, never as instructions. Render it as plain text.

event.description: The event name, for a webhook.

delivery.description: The delivery id, for a webhook.

payload.description: The input itself: a JSON object.

ProposalAction.description: One proposed action. Which fields are present depends on `kind`. Every text was masked before it was stored: secret values appear as `[masked]`. Render every text as plain text.

commit_message.description: `git_push`: the message of the pushed commit.

number.description: The pull request or issue number.

body.description: The text of a pull request, comment or review.

truncated.description: Only the first files are listed.

Proposal.description: What an automation run proposed: up to 10 actions. Immutable once stored.

base.description: With a push: the base branch.

merge_base.description: With a push: the commit the pushed commit is built on.

diff_sha256.description: With a push: the hash of the diff. What is pushed must match it.

Approval.description: The proposal of an automation run and where its approval stands. Actions before `approval_from` apply automatically; from `approval_from` on they wait for your approval.

state.description: `auto`: no action needed approval, they applied automatically. `pending`: waiting for you. `approved`, `rejected`, `expired`: what happened to it. `cancelled`: dropped without a decision (the automatic actions before it failed, the run was cancelled, or your membership no longer includes runs).

approval_from.description: Index of the first action that needs approval. `null` when none does.

proposal_sha256.description: The hash of the stored proposal. Approving in the portal binds to it.

has_diff.description: A full diff is kept (`GET /v1/runs/{id}/proposal.diff`). Only when your approval covers a push.

diff_masked.description: The kept diff contains the value of one of your secrets, shown as `[masked]`. Approving pushes the real value.

prefix_apply_run_id.description: The `apply` run of the actions before `approval_from`.

apply_run_id.description: The `apply` run of the approved actions.

next_cursor.description: Pass it as `cursor` for the next page. `null` on the last page.

Automation.description: A saved agent task. Created and edited in the portal. Never carries a secret value.

name.description: Up to 64 characters, unique among yours.

agent.description: The agent: `pi` (Pi), `pi_gentle` (Pi + Gentle Shell: Pi started through gentle-shell) or `hermes` (Hermes). Creating an automation, moving it to another workspace, changing its agent or switching it back on needs the agent installed in the workspace (`409 agent_not_installed`). If the agent is removed from the workspace later, the automation keeps it and its runs are refused with `agent_not_installed`.

instructions.description: Up to 16 KiB. Trusted: the agent follows them.

approval_kinds.description: The action kinds that wait for your approval. Empty: every action applies automatically.

approval_ttl_seconds.description: How long a proposal waits for you. 259200 (72 hours) by default.

github_repo.description: `owner/name`: the repository the actions act on.

secrets.description: The secrets its runs receive: names, variable names and who gets them. Never values.

env.description: The variable name the run sees.

exposure.description: `agent`: the agent receives it. `actions`: only the step that applies actions.

concurrency_policy.description: What happens when a new event arrives for the same pull request, issue, branch or schedule while a run for it is active, including one awaiting approval. `queue`: a new run is queued. `skip_if_active`: the new event is skipped. `supersede`: the new event starts a run and cancels the active runs of this automation for the same pull request, issue, branch or Stripe object (they end `cancelled`, with `superseded_by` set); events without such a subject (schedules, manual runs, NaN senders) behave as `queue`.

checkout.description: Where the agent works. `workspace`: in `cwd`, in your workspace, as any run. `fresh`: NaN clones `github_repo` for each run into a folder of its own, at the event's exact commit (the pull request's head commit for a `pull_request` event on that repository, the run's head commit for a `workflow_run` event on that repository, the latest commit of the default branch otherwise), and deletes it when the run ends, whatever the outcome; `cwd` is not used and `git_isolation` must be `null` or `false`. A `git_push` is refused in `fresh` mode. Needs `github_repo`.

sticky_pr_comment.description: `true`: the automation keeps one comment per pull request. Each run's `github_pr_comment` edits the comment NaN posted before for this automation instead of adding a new one. NaN only edits a comment it posted itself and marked for this automation; issue comments are never edited.

checkout_untrusted_heads.description: Only with `checkout: "fresh"`. `false` (the default): pull requests from forks, pull requests whose author has no write access to the repository (not an owner, member or collaborator) and `workflow_run` events from forks are ignored (delivery outcome `ignored`), because the agent and the tests it runs would execute that code with the automation's agent secrets in your workspace. `true`: they run too. Your decision.

AutomationTemplate.description: A template: the defaults the portal fills in when you create an automation from it.

EventFilter.description: Which webhook deliveries start a run. Every list you fill must match; empty lists match everything.

events.description: Event names (GitHub `X-GitHub-Event`, Stripe event type, NaN `X-Nan-Event`). An entry ending in `.*` matches a prefix.

Trigger.description: What starts an automation: a webhook or a schedule. The webhook URL and its signing secret are never returned after they are created or rotated.

token_prefix.description: Webhook: the start of the URL token, to recognise it.

prev_secret_until.description: After a rotation with grace: until when the previous signing secret still works.

WebhookDelivery.description: One webhook delivery. No payload and no headers are kept.

delivery_id.description: The sender's delivery id (GitHub `X-GitHub-Delivery`, Stripe event id, NaN `X-Nan-Delivery`).

input.description: Optional. A JSON object of up to 48 KiB, nested at most 8 levels. The agent receives it as untrusted data next to the instructions, never as instructions. Do not put secrets in it.

RunEventDataApprovalRequired.description: `data` of an `approval_required` event. The proposal needs your approval.

kinds.description: The kinds of the actions that wait for approval.

RunEventDataAction.description: `data` of an `action` event: one step of an `apply` run.

RunCheckout.description: The fresh checkout of a run whose automation uses `checkout: "fresh"`.

sha.description: The commit checked out. `null` until the run has resolved the default branch.

pr_number.description: The pull request, when the event was about one.

base_ref.description: The pull request's base branch, when there is one.

label.description: For display, for example `fresh @ 0123456789ab` or `fresh @ default branch`.

BadRequest.description: Invalid parameter. The body includes `param` with the offending field. Safety filter returns `content_policy_violation`. A request that does not fit the model's context window also answers `400`. On `qwen3.6` and `gemma4` the message is "Context length exceeded for model '...'" with the model's limit; on the other models it is usually that text, but it can be the generic "Invalid request. Check your request parameters.". It is not retried automatically: shorten the input or pick a model with a larger window. A `max_tokens` above what the model can generate also answers a generic `400`.

Forbidden.description: Your tier lacks access to this endpoint (`tier_restricted`). Image generation requires `inference` membership.

RateLimited.description: Rate limit exceeded: `rpm_limit` or `max_parallel_requests` (`rate_limit_exceeded`), or monthly quota exhausted (`quota_exceeded` / `insufficient_quota`).

PaymentRequired.description: The token allowance for the billing period is spent on a model that carries one, such as `glm5.3`. The request was refused before it reached the model, so nothing ran. Not retryable: the counter returns to zero when your billing period starts. The wire `code` is `cap_reached` or `monthly_cap_reached`.

error.message: Token allowance for this billing period exhausted for model glm5.3. The counter returns to zero when your next billing period starts.

RunsUnauthorized.description: Missing or invalid credentials: no `Authorization` header, an unknown or revoked API key or platform token, or an expired one (`invalid_api_key`). The message may vary.

error.message: Invalid authentication credentials. Provide a valid NaN API key in the Authorization header.
